nodes.label: PROGRESS.md — what is done, which gate, what is blocked
The first live run (2026-09-10): four defects, none caught by 382 tests
nodes.rationale: Bundled registry never read; site: ok (0 items) with nothing enabled; an invented 23:59 outranked a real Canvas deadline; the store queue deadlocked. Three lived in background.ts. Found by tracing one runtime path across parallel agents.

nodes.label: Defect: bundled registry was never read
nodes.rationale: The build copied adapters/registry.json into dist/ but only the daily GitHub fetch filled store.registry.adapters, and nothing was published there yet, so no adapter could be enabled and no item was ever labelled WEB. The worker now seeds from the bundle when the stored list is empty and logs both branches.

nodes.label: Defect: site: ok (0 items) was a lie
nodes.rationale: With no adapter enabled syncSites returned [] and the loop recorded ok — a green dot over nothing. Now raises SourceDisabled and the loop records disabled, a third branch so backoff is not armed against a source merely switched off. The old behaviour was asserted by a test.

nodes.label: Defect: an invented 23:59 outranked a real Canvas deadline
nodes.rationale: SOURCE_RANK put site above canvas assuming every instant was stated; CS 424's schedule prints a bare date, the runner filled in 23:59, and the merged HW1 row showed the invention. Needs two sources at once, so no fixture test could see it.

nodes.label: Defect: the store queue deadlocked
nodes.rationale: sync() held the queue for a whole run and called reschedule() → fireNotification(), which asked for it again; running never cleared and every later sync returned skipped until Chrome tore the worker down. ~20 minutes from wedging Sushi's machine; withStore is now re-entrant via core/queue.ts.

nodes.label: Defect: set-adapter-enabled wrote the store outside the queue
nodes.rationale: Ticking a course site during a sync was overwritten seconds later and the checkbox sprang back with no error; same for refresh-registry. Both queued now, and enabling an adapter clears the source's backoff.

nodes.label: Defect: a failing registry refresh retried on every sync
nodes.rationale: The seed leaves fetchedAt unset by design; registry.attemptedAt now rests a failure without faking a success.

nodes.label: Defect: a worker on an older build killed the settings page
nodes.rationale: TypeError on state.setAsideCourses after get-options-state came from an older worker; four sections drew and five did not, the rejection was uncaught. core/compat.ts normalizes every field a page dereferences and names the absent ones on screen; both render paths catch and report.

nodes.label: Defect: a failed fetch was reported as parse_error
nodes.rationale: The sync after a reload got TypeError: Failed to fetch for CS 424; syncSites threw ParseError whenever every adapter failed. adapterFailureKind separates structural (ParseError, 4xx) from network (failed fetch, 5xx) failures.

nodes.label: Defect: 'couldn't be read' for both parse and network failures
nodes.rationale: healthPill collapsed §6's two branches — worker rule 2's recorded example reintroduced one layer up. Now 'Gradescope didn't answer' (retryable) vs 'Canvas looks different' (needs a build), with a character budget pinned; actionFor returns a login/retry/open action for every failing state; the pill reads Checking… during a sync, capped by SYNC_SPINNER_CAP_MS because sendMessage does not reject when the worker dies.

nodes.label: Defect: the popup opened at 800×600 with the list in its left half
nodes.rationale: body max-height + overflow-y: auto removed the intrinsic height Chrome measures. Reported three times before diagnosis because the preview harness wrapped the list in a fixed-width div; npm run preview now emits preview-popup.html, the real popup with only chrome.* stubbed.

nodes.label: Defect: finished work with a late window open appeared nowhere
nodes.rationale: liveDeadline promoted a passed deadline to the late one even for submitted work, so isPast said no and visibleItems dropped the row as finished-but-not-past, and nothing drew it on its due day. isItemDone || isTickedDone now gates the promotion; merged rows need every source to agree. 925 tests passed before and after.

nodes.label: Defect: source Off but its rows still on the calendar
nodes.rationale: Two runSync branches kept a disabled source's rows, borrowing the argument for a failed source. A row is a claim some source currently reports it; a switched-off source stands behind nothing. Rows drop in both disabled branches and withoutRows applies it the moment the switch flips; overrides survive. Three tests pinned the defect.

nodes.label: Defect: the sync took the sum of its sources
nodes.rationale: The loop awaited each source in turn; with a 20 s timeout one stuck site delayed everything and the store is written once at the end, so the screen asserted the pre-sync answer throughout. Every source now starts before any is awaited, outcomes still applied in PLANS order; safe because fetches were already concurrent per host. The [sync] line carries a duration.

nodes.label: Defect: signing in changed nothing until Sync was pressed
nodes.rationale: needs_login is the only state whose fix happens where the extension cannot see it. The popup's visibilitychange only redrew a stale store; the popup-open sync was debounced 5 minutes and a backed-off source was skipped. sourcesToRecheck in core/health.ts holds the rule and a 10 s debounce, used on popup open, return to full view/Settings, and Show my calendar.

nodes.label: Defect: the debounce asked 'how long' instead of 'has anything happened'
nodes.rationale: RECHECK_AFTER_MS suppressed exactly the sign-in case it exists to serve. The worker now records the last completed navigation per source in storage.session and sourcesToRecheck treats a navigation newer than the last attempt as overriding the window; self-limiting because lastAttemptAt then exceeds the navigation. Tie decided for >= because a skipped re-check costs half an hour.

nodes.label: tabs.onUpdated as the sign-in signal
nodes.rationale: Gradescope and PrairieTest did not sync until the student clicked something and came back. tabs.onUpdated reveals a tab's URL only for hosts already permitted, needs no new permission, fires on every completed navigation, and is gated by sourcesToRecheck. core/origins.ts matches hostnames in full (endsWith would accept evilwww.gradescope.com). The privacy policy now says so.

nodes.label: Defect: the row menu opened below the fold in week view
nodes.rationale: placeFloating only opened downward; the last week row's menu opened at y=561 and ended at y=711 in a 600px window, and Hide and Merge are the third and fourth items. It now flips above the anchor; ties go downward. The month had no menu at all, so the pill is the control and joins the roving tabindex.

nodes.label: Defect: three dead redraw guards and a status line below the fold
nodes.rationale: .menu matched nothing because the class is menu-surface, so every store write or minute tick called closeMenus and a menu deleted between mousedown and mouseup swallowed the press. One MENU_SELECTOR now. reportOverride wrote to #status at the bottom of an 1100px document; it scrolls into view now.

nodes.label: Audit: 'hiding an event doesn't work on the calendar' — not found
nodes.rationale: The hide path (menu → applyOverride storing memberKeys → mutate re-running dedupe → visibleItems/groupItems/examBoard filtering) is correct. Latent hazard closed: dayContents, weekContents, monthCells and attentionGroups now filter hidden themselves. A real mechanism: a site row's content-derived sourceId changes when its title or date changes, so a hide silently stops applying.

nodes.label: Defect: every ECE 391 deadline landed six hours late
nodes.rationale: schedule.html prints the date in one cell and 'MP0 due at 18:00' in the title; the date cell stated no time, timeAssumed fired and the row went to 23:59 — a 2 h reminder would have arrived four hours after the deadline. statedTimeInText reads a cutoff anchored on 'due'; an ambiguous bare 5:00 is still refused. The adapter had been reading the landing page's office-hours table; exams.html says TBD.

nodes.label: Defect: a Gradescope course labelled stat_425_120248_268442
nodes.rationale: §5.1 declined the underscore slug (\b sees no boundary before _), so the raw string became the label and overflowed the chip. Both ends are explicit lookarounds now; the chip clips. tests/gradescope.test.ts was pinning the defect (ece_408_… asserted to yield no code). CS 498DK2 is a different case: the identity is the whole string and it stays.

nodes.label: Defect: cs124.org could not be added at all
nodes.rationale: §2.3's https://*.illinois.edu/* optional permission was incomplete when written: CS department sites are cs124.org, cs128.org, cs225.org. Widened to every https host, optional only; safe because validateAdapter requires hostPattern to name the adapter's own host exactly. Adapters naming a host the extension already holds are refused.

nodes.label: Course rename override (overrides.courseNames)
nodes.rationale: The last resort for names no rule can derive. First override storing text the student typed: renameCourse deletes on empty (a blank label would make the course vanish), capped at 60 characters, one resolver for all four surfaces, migrateOverrides and courseLabel refuse empties from older builds. Joined POPUP_STATE_FIELDS.

nodes.label: Defect: enabling a course site stayed 'Checking…' and wrote state ok by hand
nodes.rationale: Enabling wrote the flag and did not fetch; set-adapter-enabled wrote state: ok before any request (worker rule 2); Settings never listened to storage.onChanged. Goes through statusAfterEnable now and Settings redraws unless a control is focused.

nodes.label: Defect: the sources panel was clipped
nodes.rationale: A position: fixed panel contributes nothing to the document height Chrome measures, so on the short Attention tab the popup was 179px tall against a 218px panel. placeFloating now sets a temporary pixel min-height on body and, failing that, caps the panel at 600px and scrolls inside it.

nodes.label: Defect: an exam already sat counted as Overdue
nodes.rationale: An exam has no submission so isItemDone was never true and it fell through to the past branch while the Exams tab called it 'Just sat'. UX plan blocker B1.

nodes.label: Review outcome — Gradescope (12 findings, 11 fixed)
nodes.rationale: Two silent-empty paths (rows stopped matching; dashboard course cards moved) now throw; a late-only row reported the late date as dueAt; mapStatus matched by substring (Not Submitted → submitted); one bad datetime discarded the course; data-assignment-id used unvalidated. Header-based fallback implemented.

nodes.label: Review outcome — PrairieLearn (12 findings, all survived)
nodes.rationale: One unreadable popover discarded all 14 assessments; the schedule-vs-cell cross-check did not exist; positional cells[1..3] broke on an added column. Also Number('') fabricated a 0-credit tier, wallClockToIso accepted Sep 31 and 25:00, inferYear kept a rejected year. The DST path was unpinned — hard-coding -05:00 passed all 137 tests.

nodes.label: Review outcome — PrairieTest (12 findings, all survived)
nodes.rationale: A reworded card heading deleted the card's contents; isEmptyCard substring-matched the whole subtree; no duplicate-key guard in the one purely content-keyed source; date attributes accepted anything Date.parse tolerated (a bare date would fire the −24h reminder ~29h early); one unreadable value discarded the whole page.

nodes.label: Review outcome — dedupe + sync (16 findings, 7 code defects)
nodes.rationale: A source reporting ok with zero items deleted every key it had behind a green dot (now keyed on N→0); hideSubmitted hid a merged row when any member was done; the Jaccard path was badge-blind (Quiz 1 / Quiz 10 merged at 0.667); union-find could group two rows of one source; a lateDueAt-only item rendered nowhere; a disabled source lost undated items after three syncs. None of the seven was pinned by the 260 tests.

nodes.label: Review outcome — steps 9–12 (16 findings, 13 code defects)
nodes.rationale: Catch-up reminders ignored quiet hours; §7 read dueAt alone so reduced-credit deadlines got no reminder; unserialized whole-store writes re-fired notifications and reverted hides; validateAdapter accepted a hostPattern broader than the adapter's host; an adapter with a broken title selector returned []; hiddenItemIds keyed by Item.id was spent on merge; notification click targets lived in worker memory.

nodes.label: Tier 0a (2026-09-10, 13 items)
nodes.rationale: pending state and core/health.ts with a toolbar badge; catch-up reminders fixed; moved deadlines re-arm and say so; late windows listed on their own instant in amber; invented 23:59 no longer shown as a clock; doneKeys; not-for-credit chipped; core/quality.ts surfaces unparsed* flags; Settings tidy; a new build lifts backoff; adapter date grammar; migrate validates raw and items; Copy diagnostics and Report this page. 388 → 546 tests.

nodes.label: Tier 0b (4 of 7 done)
nodes.rationale: Repo public and registry URL live (adapters reach every install within a day); beta install kit (npm run package, INSTALL.txt, beta-install.md); ECE 310 adapter; Canvas term filter. Not started: non-CS first look, PL/PT 'not used by you', first-run page; G4 is Sushi's.

nodes.label: UX plan phases A–G (2026-09-12)
nodes.rationale: A trust and correctness (sat exam, contrast tokens, names.ts, view caps, real-document preview); B primitives and icons; C popup IA (agenda, rolling week, one health pill, 145px of chrome); D Settings navigation; E first run and install (opensOnInstall, pin card, setupSummary); F notifications lead with the work; G store readiness (icon A, version 1.0.0, generated screenshots).

nodes.label: smartPhysics as a fifth source
nodes.rationale: For PHYS 211–214, whose 8:00 AM deadlines a 11:59 PM habit misses. A source, not an adapter, because every course page is addressed by a per-student enrolment id; two-stage plan like Gradescope; off by default. The capture is a Fall 2025 course, so the parser has never seen a live term.

nodes.label: Adapter.columns — header-driven column lookup
nodes.rationale: Reads a table's own header row instead of counting cells (parser rule 3 in declarative form), making a table-shaped course page a five-minute job. Stops short of autodetection: ECE 310's 'Assessment Due' column holds HW1.

nodes.label: Never-signed-in detection for Gradescope and PrairieTest
nodes.rationale: Both answer 200 at the unchanged URL when the student has never signed in, so the parsers threw and the UI showed a red dot with nothing to click. Marker for Gradescope is js-logInButton, absent from the signed-in capture.

nodes.label: Amendment §4.1/§5.3: Canvas course_code is an opaque slug
nodes.rationale: course_code is cs_357_120268_263847, not 'CS 225'; §5.1 runs against name and courseLabel must not use course_code. The finding applied to Gradescope too, which has no name field.

nodes.label: Amendment §4.1: no while(1); prefix on this deployment
nodes.rationale: Keep the detection, don't require it.

nodes.label: Amendment §4.3: credit table has a header row and no tbody
nodes.rationale: The 0-credit row's End is an em dash, not empty; lateDueAt must skip a 0-credit tier. The access-details table is present in the fetched HTML (§12.1 resolved).

nodes.label: Amendment §4.4: PrairieTest links and machine-readable dates
nodes.rationale: The booked row links to /pt/student/reservation/{id} with no exam id; the available row's button links to /pt/student/exam/{id}. Both instants are JSON in data-format-date / data-format-date-range, so neither regex nor year inference is needed; the visible text is not a fixed format. One empty-card wording per card; a third card exists.

nodes.label: Amendment §4.2/§3.1: Gradescope row is a button before submission and an a after
nodes.rationale: Both carry data-assignment-id. The hidden Due Date column is state-dependent and must not be used as dueAt.

nodes.label: Amendment §5.3: an assumed time is the last resort, not the first
nodes.rationale: parseAdapterDateParts reports timeAssumed, the runner records it in extra, and dedupe prefers any member with a stated instant, falling back to an assumed one only when it is the only instant. A site that prints a real time still outranks Canvas.

nodes.label: Amendment §5.3 (step 7): a single badge token can satisfy the subset rule
nodes.rationale: The ≥2-token subset rule rejected both pairs the spec cites (Lab 3 / Lab 3 Report; Homework 3 / HW3 …) because §5.2 collapses them to one token. Accepting a lone badge token is a trade: {mp2} can merge into {mp2, checkpoint}, and GA 0 / GA00 collapse to one token. Survivable because of the same-source group check. Unexercised by G3; G4's job.

nodes.label: Amendment §3: hides and done ticks are keyed by memberKeys, not Item.id
nodes.rationale: An id is a hash of the member set, so a hide keyed by it is spent the moment the row merges with anything; member keys are pruned by §5.4 like every other override.

nodes.label: Decision: Canvas concluded-course filter via include[]=term
nodes.rationale: The real term carries dates while a stale course's OPEN term has null start and end. Keep courses whose term brackets today, set aside unbounded-term courses only when a current term exists, fail open otherwise. Options › Courses › Older courses lists what was held back with Put back.

nodes.label: Fixtures captured
nodes.rationale: Canvas courses/planner/assignments JSON (planner-items.json real with one dated row since Sep 10); Gradescope dashboard + course-1352838; PrairieLearn assessments-cs357 with all 8 popovers; course site cs424 schedule (401 in place); PrairieTest two home captures a week apart.

nodes.label: The one source with no login page (course sites)
nodes.rationale: LOGIN_URL has no entry for site. The adapter URL that answered 401 is recorded as SourceStatus.loginUrl (the requested URL, not finalUrl, which is mid-SAML) and actionFor falls back to it. Four surfaces each decided what a sign-in link is; they go through one signInUrl now.

nodes.label: The store documents, aligned and published
nodes.rationale: The privacy policy told students four sites while the manifest asked for five; it is now derived from the same source origins, permissions and registry host as the listing, generated by scripts/site.mjs and live at sushelan.github.io/illini-dash/privacy.html. docs/pre-submit.md holds the clean-profile and G4 walks.

nodes.label: Light or dark is a setting (is-dark class)
nodes.rationale: Dark values lived behind a media query that no choice could override; the stylesheet keys on one class resolved by resolveDark(mode, systemPrefersDark). Light surfaces became a blue ramp; tokens.test.ts computes contrast for all six palettes.

nodes.label: Export .ics moved to the bar
nodes.rationale: A calendar icon in both windows; src/ui/download.ts holds the one answer to which items go in the file. The sixth control cost 13px, recovered from icons and padding. A self-updating .ics is a subscription and needs a server the project deliberately has none of.

nodes.label: Open full view reuses one tab
nodes.rationale: The popup is destroyed on focus loss so the worker owns the tab id in chrome.storage.session; tabs.get/update need no tabs permission; the view is handed over through localStorage.

nodes.label: Shared parser primitives (src/core/parsing.ts)
nodes.rationale: parseField, KeyGuard, sameOriginHttpsUrl, looksLoggedOut, isInstant, nonEmpty, textOf — rules previously written three or four times and reintroduced as defects, each now pinned by tests from several source test files.

nodes.label: VERIFY: does PrairieTest render the available card for a student with no CBTF courses?
nodes.rationale: Both captures come from an account that has them; a missing card is a ParseError, so a non-CBTF beta tester might see a spurious red dot. Check at G4.

hyperedges.label: Spec amendments forced by real data (parser rule 9: the capture beats the spec)
